newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMAN FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMAN FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND PROGRAMME.

text.p: Programme of matches in the German first division at the weekend.
Duisburg have not won at home since the re-start after the winter break in mid-February and are very close to relegation zone. They have also not beaten Karlsruhe at home since 1991-92 season.

This Hamburg derby is always full of emotion and both teams are in the second half of the table and need points. Relegation-threatened St Pauli have taken just one point from their last six games and have never beaten Hamburg at home in the Bundesliga. A win would set off wild celebrations among their fanatical supporters.

The big match of the weekend. Dortmund are in a groove after taking three-point lead at the top with 3-0 victory over Hansa Rostock in midweek. Stuttgart hit five past Cologne on Tuesday and four past Hamburg last week. Stuttgart have not scored at home against Dortmund in the last two seasons but it would be a surprise if their attacking team fail to find the net this time.

Until last Sunday Bayern had lost just one game all season. But a 5-2 defeat by Bayer Leverkusen last weekend and a 2-0 loss at Armenia Bielefeld on Wednesday has rocked the club. Schalke have not scored against Bayern in Munich's Olympic stadium in the last three seasons but have an excellent record away this term.

Leverkusen take on promoted Bielefeld after a mixed week. Sunday's 5-2 thrashing of Bayern was followed by a 3-0 defeat at 1860 Munich on Wednesday. This could be a tight game. Leverkusen have won their last four home games but Bielefeld are undefeated away from home since the winter break.

Freiburg are looking doomed to second division football next season, already five points adrift at the bottom. 1860 have a superb chance to pick up away points which could take them up the table and closer to a UEFA Cup place next season.
A battle in the bottom half of the table with few goals expected. Rostock have yet to score at home since the winter break. Duesseldorf have not scored away since the re-start.

Moenchengladbach have lifted their form at home in the last few games and need a win to get away from the relegation zone. Cologne looking to bounce back from 5-1 thrashing at home by Stuttgart in midweek.

Promoted Bochum have enjoyed a good season so far and are almost certain of keeping their place in the Bundesliga. Both teams are level on points and still in a position to make a challenge for a place in the UEFA Cup next season.
